Draftpad: Dear members of the Brook Lane allotment group,
At the meeting last Sunday we agreed to share the new water tank between the twelve plots on the lower field. This letter sets out what we decided, so that people who were not there know the plan.

The tank holds 1,500 litres and sits next to the shed by the east gate. The town grant paid for the tank and the pipe, which cost 860 pounds in total. Each plot gets a key for the tap. Please keep the key on your own key ring and do not leave it in the shed.

From May to September, please water only before ten in the morning or after six in the evening. The tank fills from the roof of the shed, and it empties fast on hot afternoons. If the level falls below the red mark, use a watering can and not the hose until it rains again.

We also agreed on a rota for the compost bays. Each pair of plots turns the compost for one week. The list is on the shed door and starts with plots 1 and 2 in the first week of April. If you cannot do your week, swap with another pair and write the change on the list.

Rosalind Achebe offered to collect money for a second tank next year. A second tank would let the upper field use rain water too. She suggests 15 pounds from each plot, paid by the end of June. Tell her at the next meeting if you agree or have another idea.
The next meeting is on the first Sunday of May at eleven, in the shed if it rains and by the pond if it is dry. Bring a cup.
